models.invariant: Each left box is one elementary outcome, not an equally weighted observation. An arrow ends at the boundary of its mapped-value box.
code: Start with all outcome weights.
Select one outcome and its fixed image.
Add its mass to that image fiber.
Check that the output masses still sum to one.

models.title: CDF construction: left limit versus included atom
models.invariant: All thresholds use one fixed real axis. Each closed endpoint includes its atom; the open endpoint records the value just before it.
code: Sort distinct atoms and merge any duplicates.
Add one positive atom mass.
Extend the right-continuous plateau.
Compare F(x) and F(x−).

teaching.operation: Finish one failure prefix with a success
teaching.why: Earlier failures and the final success are different requirements. Memorylessness holds only when the per-trial hazard remains constant.
teaching.reading: Displayed prefix probabilities retain their true masses. The omitted tail remains explicit; no prefix is renormalized.
guide: Start with survival probability one.
Require failure at each earlier trial.
Multiply current survival by the current success probability.
Update the remaining survival tail.

models.title: Capped stopping: success and censoring merge at the cap
models.invariant: At the last permitted time, the variable stops whether success occurs or not. The last mass is survival to the cap, not success at the cap.
code: Require a failed prefix before each earlier stop.
Assign a success mass at times below the cap.
At the cap, merge success and censoring branches.
Check that the capped law is normalized.

models.title: No boys: likelihood reweights a countable family-size law
models.invariant: Original size masses multiply no-boy likelihood 2^(−n). The exact evidence mass is 2/3. The finite display retains explicit prior and posterior tails.
code: Keep the original geometric family-size law.
Multiply each mass by its no-boy likelihood.
Use the exact infinite evidence sum, 2/3.
Divide weighted masses by the evidence.

teaching.reading: Independent equal-probability trials update a count law by failure and success branches. Fixed final axes expose which coefficients belong to which count.
guide: Initialize probability one at count zero.
Extend each current count through a failure branch.
Extend it through a success branch.
Merge branches arriving at the same new count.

Force the last trial to be a success.
Choose r−1 earlier success positions.
Multiply each valid path probability by its position count.
